name: 5,5-Dimethyl-6'-aminooxyluciferin
reason: oxyluciferin emitter model, outside the agreed substrate-analogue scope
note: Insoluble and unstable in water, so no aqueous data. Strong fluorescence solvatochromism (e.g. 494 nm in p-xylene to 607 nm in methanol for 3a). Its fluorescence in 2-propanol (593 nm) matches the bioluminescence maximum of aminoluciferin with Ppy luciferase (595 nm).

name: 5,5-Dimethyl-6'-dimethylaminooxyluciferin
reason: oxyluciferin emitter model, outside the agreed substrate-analogue scope
note: Insoluble and unstable in water, so no aqueous data. Strong fluorescence solvatochromism (e.g. 494 nm in p-xylene to 607 nm in methanol for 3a). Its fluorescence in acetonitrile (621 nm) matches the bioluminescence maximum of 6'-dimethylaminoluciferin (620 nm). These matches are the basis of the Hirano/Maki 'use the luciferin's own fluorescence to predict lambda_BL' rule that underpins the design
